newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Service downplays Rose Hill deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Service downplays Rose Hill deal.

text.p: The president of Service Corp International on Friday downplayed an acquisition announced earlier by target Loewen Group Inc, saying that the deal represents "no real victory" for Loewen shareholders.
"We don't see how that's a 'win' situation," president William Heiligbrodt told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He also said that Service Corp's unsolicited bid for Loewen makes sense for shareholders of both companies, noting that Service Corp is continuing to weigh its options.
Service Corp on Tuesday disclosed an unsolicited bid for Loewen valued at $2.8 billion, excluding $1.3 billion in debt. Loewen has said it is evaluating the offer.
Heiligbrodt declined to say whether the company would launch a hostile takeover of Loewen, only noting "we usually try to finish the things we start."
"We have a game plan and we're just starting," he added.
When asked if Service Corp would consider a role for top management of Loewen if a friendly deal were completed, he said "we'd certainly like to talk about that."

Heiligbrodt said he has had no contact with Loewen since publicly disclosing the $43 per share offer for the Canadian company. In a letter to Loewen chief executive Raymond Loewen, Heiligbrodt said he had tried to reach the company several times since September 11, but calls were not returned.
On Friday, loewen annoucned an agreement with Blackstone Capital Partners to buy Rose Hill Memorial Park Association and Rose Hills Co Inc for $240 million.
Service Corp is the nation's largest funeral home chain and competes fiercely with number-two Loewen.
Although the size of both companies has raised some concern on Wall Street about potential antitrust issues, Heiligbrodt indicated a belief that those could be overcome.
"We've looked at that and we certainly think this transaction is do-able. That was one of our first considerations," he said.
Industry experts have speculated that any potential transaction would probably require some divestitures of properties.

Heiligbrodt declined to comment on Wall Street estimates that Service Corp could pay as much as $50 per share without dilution to 1997 earnings. The company has indicated that it would be willing to raise its offer for Loewen if it receives access to Loewen's financial records.
"We have our own set of numbers. We intend to pay a fair price for Loewen. We're not in this to get any gigantic bargain," Heiligbrodt said.
He also downplayed a Canadian newspaper report in which a Loewen executive said institutional investors thought the offer was "very light."
"We haven't had any (shareholders) tell us that," Heiligbrodt said.
